chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Minhal al-Qassab together from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever gains wealth from four sources, it will not be accepted from him in four: whoever gains wealth from embezzlement, usury, betrayal, or theft, it will not be accepted from him in zakat, charity, Hajj, or Umra. And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not accept a Hajj or an Umra from forbidden wealth.

key_terms.خيانة: Betrayal / treachery — breach of trust in financial dealings
key_terms.ربا: Usury (riba) — interest-bearing financial transactions, forbidden in Islam
key_terms.سرقة: Theft — unlawful taking of another's property
key_terms.غلول: Embezzlement (ghulul) — misappropriating communal or war spoils
key_terms.مال حرام: Forbidden wealth — money acquired through unlawful means

ai.seo_question: Can forbidden wealth be used for Hajj, zakat, or charity in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) establishes a fundamental Islamic financial-legal principle: wealth obtained through four illicit means — embezzlement, usury, betrayal, and theft — cannot be used for four acts of worship: zakat, charity, Hajj, and Umra. He further emphasizes that God does not accept any Hajj or Umra funded by forbidden wealth. This ruling, from the assembly of 368 AH, underscores the inseparability of financial ethics and spiritual worship in Islam.
